en.hubeali:
And by his chain that, 
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, a man came over to him<sup>asws</sup> so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! A robber came and stole my wife’s ornaments’.
So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But if he had come over to a son of a righteous woman, he would not have been pleased with that until he had driven him away with the sword’.
en.sarwar: 3. The narrator of the previous through his chain of narrators has said the following: “Once a man came to Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said, ’O Amir al-Mu’minin, a thief entered in the house of my wife and stole her ornaments.
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Had he (the thief) entered the house of the son of a clean woman he would not agree with less than overwhelming him (thief) by his sword.’”
